ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering Law No. 80 of 2002, as amended, including Laws No. 78 of 2003, 181 of 2008, 36 of 2014, 8 of 2015, 64 of 2020, and subsequent amendments; Executive Regulations issued by Prime Ministerial Decree No. 951 of 2003, as amended; Companies Law No. 159 of 1981, as amended, and its Executive Regulations issued by Ministerial Decree No. 96 of 1982, as amended; Egyptian Financial Regulatory Authority and General Authority for Investment and Free Zones rules requiring maintenance and disclosure of ownership, control, management, and beneficial-owner information. Egypt does not operate a generally open public UBO register equivalent to a fully public central register; applicable UBO information is maintained by regulated entities, competent authorities, and relevant registries under sectoral AML/CFT and company-law rules.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Screen every shareholder, UBO, director, manager, authorized signatory, intermediary, bank, supplier, customer, and controlling entity before incorporation and periodically thereafter against United Nations Security Council sanctions, applicable Egyptian domestic sanctions and terrorism lists, OFAC lists where a U.S. nexus or dollar clearing exists, EU and UK lists where contract or banking risk warrants, and reputable PEP, relatives-and-close-associates, adverse-media, and enforcement databases. Apply enhanced due diligence, senior-management approval, source-of-wealth verification, transaction monitoring, and documented escalation for PEPs, sanctioned-party matches, high-risk jurisdictions, opaque nominee structures, cash-intensive activity, and unexplained third-party payments. Do not rely on a 25% ownership test alone: identify control through voting rights, appointment rights, contractual control, or other means.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) official electronic services and incorporation portal, supported by GAFI's Investor Services Center
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be distinguishable from existing registered names, must not mislead the public regarding business activity, status, nationality, governmental affiliation, or regulated-sector authorization, and must comply with GAFI and Companies Law requirements. An Arabic name or Arabic transliteration is generally required for Egyptian registration records; a Latin or English trading presentation may be used only where accepted by GAFI and must not create a separate legal identity. The name should be checked in Arabic and English transliteration, including phonetic equivalents and abbreviations.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Egyptian government, ministry, authority, public institution, armed forces, police, central bank, or other governmental references without written approval
Bank, banking, finance, insurance, securities, investment fund, exchange, payment, electronic money, microfinance, or similar regulated-sector terms without the applicable regulator's approval

University, hospital, medical, pharmaceutical, energy, petroleum, mining, aviation, shipping, tourism, security, media, telecommunications, and similar regulated or licensed-sector terms without required approval
International, national, Arab, Egyptian, royal, presidential, diplomatic, or other prestige or geographic terms where their use implies official status or requires prior clearance
Names identical or confusingly similar to an existing company, registered trademark, trade name, or protected governmental designation
Words or expressions contrary to public order, public morals, or Egyptian law
Religious, political, military, or diplomatic designations implying official affiliation
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Obtain the written or electronic rejection reason from GAFI; preserve the application number, proposed names, payment receipt, and search results; submit a corrected name or replacement names through the GAFI portal or Investor Services Center within the reservation period; where the applicant contests the rejection, file a reasoned administrative grievance with the competent GAFI office and, if necessary, pursue the applicable administrative-law challenge before the competent Egyptian administrative court. A rejection appeal does not suspend the reservation period unless GAFI confirms an extension. Conduct trademark and trade-name searches separately because GAFI name clearance does not establish trademark ownership.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A registered address in Egypt is required for company registration, tax registration, official notices, books and records, and regulatory correspondence. A serviced or virtual office may be accepted for a holding, administrative, or low-activity entity if the provider supplies a valid lease or occupancy document and permits official inspection and receipt of notices. It is not a sufficient substitute for operational substance for an apparel liquidation trading business where inventory, import documentation, employees, warehouse arrangements, customer records, and banking activity are expected. A separate compliant warehouse, logistics facility, or third-party logistics agreement may be required depending on the actual model and customs position.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Estimated 10%–20% annual likelihood of an unannounced or short-notice physical verification for a newly formed ordinary trading LLC, increasing to approximately 25%–40% during the first registration or tax-verification cycle if the entity uses a virtual office, reports material turnover, imports goods, claims VAT positions, has inconsistent address data, or presents elevated AML indicators. These are risk estimates, not statutory probabilities or official government statistics.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Law No. 159 of 1981, as amended, Articles 48-53 (Limited Liability Company formation rules); supplemented by Investment Law No. 72 of 2017, Article 13, and Executive Regulations (Ministerial Decree No. 96/2018).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: GAFI – General Authority for Investment and Free Zones, Companies Registration Department, One-Stop Shop, Ministry of Investment and International Cooperation, Cairo.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Memorandum of Association and Articles of Association (Aqd al-Sharika / Contract of Incorporation).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital prescribed for LLCs in Law 159/1981; the shareholders freely set the quota share capital. Cash contributions must be fully deposited in the company's 'under-formation' bank account before notarial certification; the bank deposit certificate must accompany the incorporation application. Statutory escrow is not required for this wholesale trading activity.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that each subscriber to the Memorandum of Association of the Egyptian limited liability company adopts the share subscription schedule; the subscribed quota shares represent 100% of the paid-up capital of EGP 50,000 divided into equal quota shares. RESOLVED, that the registered office be fixed at the address specified in the Memorandum of Association, Cairo Governorate. RESOLVED, that [Name], [Nationality], be appointed General Manager for a three-year term, with full authority to open and operate bank accounts, execute contracts, hire staff, represent the company before GAFI and tax authorities. RESOLVED, that [Name] be appointed compliance officer to maintain the statutory register. All acts already performed in furtherance of the formation are hereby ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Legal name reservation and feasibility clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI e-services One-Stop Shop (new investors portal), Cairo
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an online name reservation application in Arabic with up to three proposed trade names, stating the primary activity as ISIC 4641 wholesale of finished garments. Pay the nominal electronic fee; obtain the automated name certificate before drafting the notarial deed.
required_dossiers: Passport copies of individual shareholders or directors
Signed incorporation application naming a provisional manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a name is rejected, activate the second or third proposed name in the same reservation file. For higher priority disputes, submit a written rectification to GAFI's Commercial Names Committee; the committee must decide within 10 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of under-formation bank account and capital deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Egyptian commercial bank (e.g., National Bank of Egypt, Commercial International Bank)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the name certificate and draft Memorandum, open a blocked under-formation account in the LLC's name. Deposit the entire cash quota capital; obtain a bank deposit certificate expressly stating that the amount is held for the LLC under formation and is in line with the drawn-up capital figure.
required_dossiers: Passport copies of founder(s) and appointed manager
Copy of the proposed registered-office lease or address proof
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank questions the clients' identity or the source of funds, provide certified passport translations and evidence of trade reference. Any mismatch between the deposit certificate and the capital clause in the Memorandum must be corrected before notarization.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of the Memorandum of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Office of the Notary General, Ministry of Justice; local Notary Public Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All founders or their appointed representatives appear before the Notary Public to sign and authenticate the Memorandum of Association in Arabic. The notary verifies the identity documents, the name certificate, the capital deposit certificate, and the lease address, then numbers and seals the incorporation deed and returns the certified copies to the parties.
required_dossiers: Name certificate and bank capital deposit certificate
Six copies of the Arabic Memorandum of Association
Founder passport copies and power-of-attorney for any foreign founder
Registered office lease or title deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: For a notarial objection, amend the non-material defects and re-file within 5 business days with a covering letter. If wrongful rejection is detected, escalate to the head of the Notary General office or apply to the competent administrative court for a forced notarial approval.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Companies Registration Department / One-Stop Shop (physical counter or online portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized Memorandum together with the capital deposit certificate, name certificate, lease, and founder identification to the GAFI registrar. The registrar completes statutory review, checks compliance with Companies Law 159/1981 and Investment Law 72/2017, then issues the Certificate of Establishment and the company's Commercial Registration proof.
required_dossiers: Registered office lease or notarized usufruct
Completed GAFI registration form (sample available at the One-Stop Shop)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If GAFI issues a query, respond in writing within 10 business days and resubmit the corrected file. Upon rejection, the company may request the GAFI internal complaints committee to re-examine the file; judicial review through the Administrative Court is available within 30 days of a written refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Registry entry and tax file registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Commercial Registry (competent First Instance Court location) and the District Tax Office (Ministry of Finance)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the GAFI certificate, apply at the Commercial Registry office for the index entry record, trade register extract, and company file number. Then proceed to the relevant District Tax Office to obtain the Tax Card; register for VAT and payroll tax where thresholds are met. This step also opens the corporate governance file and fixes the company's primary tax seat.
required_dossiers: Lease or title deed for registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Commercial Registry or Tax Office requests clarifications, provide the missing attachments and pay the fixed amendment fee. A late-registration tax penalty may be appealed under Article 48 of Law 91/2005 to the Internal Tax Complaint Committee within 30 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - this ISIC 4641 activity constitutes wholesale trading, not factory production; the General Authority for Industrial Control (GAIC) has no jurisdiction over the warehouse unless the premises itself requires a construction authorization. If the warehouse exceeds 250 sqm, the Governorate's Directorate of Housing may issue a building-function certificate.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No industrial operating license is required. The company's operating permit is the Commercial Registry Extract issued under Law 34/1976 as the governing trade authorization for wholesale apparel trading.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA) under Law 4/1994 and its Executive Regulations
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - Category D, non-industrial commercial activity; no environmental screening or full EIA report required for warehousing and off-price wholesale trading of finished garments.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater or stack emissions; municipal waste from packaging must be segregated and disposed through a registered solid-waste contractor in accordance with Governorate Decree No. 88/2016. Air conditioning and refrigeration units at the office/warehouse must not use chlorofluorocarbon refrigerants banned under Egypt's Ozone Depletion Regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: A fire safety clearance from the Civil Defense Department (Ministry of Interior) is required before the warehouse receives goods if the storage area exceeds 250 sqm; the clearance verifies escape paths, fire extinguishers, and electrical wiring integrity. An electrical installation certificate and an occupational health clearance under Law 12/2003 (Labor Law) must be kept on file. For non-industrial office-only sites, a municipal physical-presence inspection by the district's licensing unit may be mandatory before the Commercial Registry confirms the address.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) – official name: Misr El-Mehwar for Tax Administration; corporate and VAT registration portal: https://www.incometax.gov.eg; e-invoicing portal: https://www.invoice.bambooroute.eta.gov.eg; VAT returns portal: https://eta.gov.eg
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The foreign entity must incorporate as an Egyptian LLC (branch or standalone), obtain a commercial record (CR) from the General Authority for Investment (GAFI), then register with the Egyptian Tax Authority within 30 days of commencing business to obtain the Tax Card (TIN) and VAT registration certificate. Required documents include the CR, share register, lease contract, power of attorney, passport copies of shareholders, board resolution, and proof of office address. Tax ID is issued in paper form and activated in ETA’s e-system; VAT registration must be completed before issue of tax invoices.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or pass-through election exists for Egyptian LLCs. Corporations are taxed at the entity level only; shareholders are taxed on dividends through withholding. There is no domestic hybrid-mismatch election, and Egypt does not apply US-style check-the-box rules. However, a small or micro business may elect simplified taxation under Income Tax Law No. 91 of 2005 (as amended by Law 14/2018) if turnover is below EGP 20 million. No other material elections are available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under Law No. 67 of 2016
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 annual taxable turnover (Art. 19, VAT Law 67/2016). A foreign person opening a permanent establishment or performing taxable economic activity in Egypt must register irrespective of turnover if supplies are deemed Egyptian.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory real-time e-invoicing clearance through the Egyptian Tax Authority’s (ETA) e-invoice platform. All registered taxpayers must integrate business systems with the ETA API, upload invoice XML/JSON files before dispatch, and receive a unique tax invoice ID and two-dimensional barcode (QR) validated by the ETA. Invoices without ETA clearance and QR stamp are considered invalid evidence for tax deduction. E-receipt requirements apply to retail sellers. Phased implementation has reached large and medium taxpayers; full mandatory application to all VAT registrants is enforced.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Article 32 of Law 67/2016 zero-rates exported goods where title passes to a non-resident, the goods are physically transported out of Egypt within the statutory period, and export occurs under a valid customs export declaration. Offshore services and related supplies physically performed and used outside Egypt may be zero-rated when received by a non-resident. The exporter must hold documentary evidence of actual export and hard-currency proceeds.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Inward Remittance Certificate (IRS issued by Egyptian bank proving FX proceeds received)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The ETA may conduct post-export desk audits with full inspection of customs, shipping, and bank remittance records. If zero-rating is disallowed, the taxpayer must pay the 14% VAT with late additions from the date of export; a penalty not exceeding 100% of tax is applicable under Law 67/2016. Fraudulent export-zero-rating claims may trigger criminal sanctions including imprisonment, fines of up to EGP 1 million, and forfeiture of rights to export relief. Retrospective assessment limitation is generally 5 years, or 6 years in fraud cases.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) — Al-Bank al-Markazi al-Misri; competent supervisory authority for all foreign-exchange operations under the Central Bank and Banking System Law No. 194 of 2020, acting through its Foreign Exchange Committee.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt has accepted IMF Article VIII obligations since 1997, so current-account transactions, including profit and dividend remittances, are formally unrestricted. Following the 6 March 2024 unification of the exchange rate, the EGP/USD rate is determined by the interbank market. Convertibility is subject to administrative documentation and bank-side compliance rather than CBE pre-approval. Profit remittance requires audited financial statements demonstrating distributable retained earnings, a valid tax clearance certificate, and the instructing bank's sanctions, PEP, and source-of-funds screening.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under CBE foreign-exchange instructions and the Executive Regulations of Law No. 194 of 2020, export proceeds must be received into an Egyptian bank account within 180 days of the bill-of-lading date. Following the March 2024 float, the mandatory conversion ratio is 0%; exporters may retain proceeds in foreign-currency accounts or convert at the prevailing interbank rate. Failure to repatriate within the statutory window triggers CBE penalties, suspension of trade facilities, and customs export-compliance review.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Operational Account (USD and EGP)
Trade Finance Facility Account / LC Settlement
USD Clearing Account / Swift Transfer Hub

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low — no passporting right exists for foreign e-money institutions in Egypt. Under Law No. 194 of 2020, only CBE-licensed banks and licensed payment service providers may hold funds, operate payment accounts, or execute EGP/USD conversion in the onshore market. Offshore digital EMIs cannot access the CBE clearing systems (RTGS/EgySI) or maintain settlement accounts. A licensed local PSP partnership (for example Paymob or Fawry) is feasible only for low-value retail collections and is not suitable for wholesale trade settlement, letter-of-credit disbursements, or export proceeds repatriation.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Egyptian banks generally require at least one authorized signatory and the ultimate beneficial owner to attend an in-person compliance interview at the branch during corporate account opening; fully remote onboarding is not available. Non-resident directors may be represented by an in-country attorney holding a notarized power-of-attorney that is apostilled (Hague Apostille Convention effective for Egypt on 14 March 2022) or consular-legalized. The interview covers business model, source of funds, expected payment flows, counterparty jurisdictions, and confirmation that settlement will be fully bank-traced with no cash collection.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Value mismatch and invoice gaps in off-price liquidation purchases, indicating trade-based money laundering (TBML) risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Brand-authorization letters from liquidators; original purchase invoices and bulk-buyer agreements; bills of lading with CargoX ACI declarations and valid ACID numbers; independent off-price valuation benchmarks; inventory aging reports; and two years of clean bank references from prior jurisdictions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque ultimate beneficial ownership involving non-resident members not disclosed in Egyptian Commercial Registry filings.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized certificate of incorporation; MOA/AOA with full shareholder schedule; current Commercial Registry extract; signed UBO declaration; apostilled or consular-legalized board resolutions appointing directors and signatories; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds statements for each material shareholder.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity payables and receivables to MENA and Sub-Saharan African counterparties that intersect sanctions or PEP screening.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete counterparty KYC packs; negative-news and sanctions-screening exception memos; transport and customs evidence for each trade lane; declared monthly settlement forecast; and transaction-monitoring protocols accepted by the bank's AML unit.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cash-heavy off-price collection flows perceived as circumventing Egypt's promoted electronic-payment rails for commercial transactions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board-adopted policy prohibiting cash settlement; evidence of all collections through official bank transfers; reconciled sales ledgers; ERP treasury extracts; and external audit confirmation of the cash-free disbursement cycle.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital contribution routed via SWIFT MT103 to the EG_LLC beneficiary account with a tier-1 Egyptian bank, with narrative explicitly stating equity subscription to EG_LLC and identifying the CBE balance-of-payments statistical purpose for inward direct investment. The receiving bank requires a current Commercial Registry extract, certificate of incorporation, tax card, board resolution authorizing the capital increase, and the subscribed-shareholder schedule. No CBE prior approval is required; the bank files the external-transaction report and credits funds either to a USD account or converts at the interbank market rate.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Effective from the 6 March 2024 CBE circular, Egypt no longer imposes a mandatory letter-of-credit rule; licensed banks may clear outbound import and trade payments via (a) SWIFT MT103 direct transfer against invoice documents; (b) documentary collections (D/P and D/A); and (c) MT700 sight or usance commercial letters of credit. Every consignment must be registered in the CargoX ACI single window with an ACID number, and the settling bank will require the commercial invoice, packing list, GOEIC importer-registration evidence, and proof of the ACI declaration before releasing foreign exchange.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable onshore EGP/USD foreign-exchange forward contracts, trade-backed, with maximum tenor of 12 months, executed through a CBE-licensed bank.
EGP/USD cross-currency swaps with a licensed bank under a documented ISDA/CSA framework for balance-sheet hedging.
Onshore FX swaps (spot versus forward) to bridge timing mismatches between export receipts and import payments.
Offshore EGP NDFs and onshore NDFs are not permissible settlement or hedging instruments for Egyptian-resident entities; only deliverable forward contracts and swaps may be booked.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Tax Form 41) with audited financial statements annexed
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) – Corporate Tax Department
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within four months after the fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year LLC by 30 April of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment surcharge of 2% per month (or fraction thereof) on unpaid tax; administrative late-filing penalties up to EGP 2,000,000; enforced tax lien and collection procedures; criminal liability for tax evasion; persistent non-filing may lead to ETA deregistration and ultimately administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Commercial Register Renewal of the LLC
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Register Office, Ministry of Trade and Industry (GAFI register for Investment Law projects)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually before the expiry date of the commercial-register certificate; renewal window opens 60 days before the anniversary date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-renewal fines per the Commercial Registry fee schedule; suspension of registration for continued default; prolonged non-compliance beyond approximately one year may trigger administrative strike-off by the Companies Authority.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Ordinary General Assembly; Approval and Deposit of Audited Financial Statements, Auditor's Report, and Minutes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Companies Authority / General Authority for Investment (GAFI) Commercial Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: AGM must be convened within 6 months of the fiscal year-end (by 30 June for a 31 December fiscal year); minutes and approved financial statements filed within 30 days after the AGM
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Corporate contravention fines under Companies Law 159/1981; unlawful distributions if financial statements are not approved; sustained default may trigger registry strike-off and personal liability of managers.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership (UBO) Confirmation and AML Register Update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit (EMLCU) through the AML-supervised authority and Companies Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually in parallel with the commercial-register renewal cycle and within 30 days after any change in direct or indirect beneficial ownership; annual nil-change confirmation remains mandatory
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative AML fines and DNFBP supervisory sanctions for stale or inaccurate UBO records; criminal penalties for intentionally false declarations; persistent non-compliance may lead to disqualification of managers and strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Employer Payroll and Withholding Tax Monthly Remittances and Annual Final Reconciliation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) – Withholding Tax Department
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly withholding returns by the 15th of the following month; annual employer reconciliation filed within the statutory window after the calendar year-end (typically by end of February)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 2% monthly delay penalty on unremitted withheld tax; employer jointly and severally liable for employee tax; criminal sanctions under Law 91/2005 for wilful failure to withhold.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Periodic Value Added Tax Returns and Annual Closing / Input-VAT Reconciliation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly returns due by the 15th of the month following each taxable period; quarterly cash-basis option for eligible small taxpayers; annual stock and input-VAT reconciliation appended to the January-period return of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: VAT delay fines and late-payment penalties; disallowed input VAT for incomplete records or incorrect documentation; criminal liability for fraudulent invoice issuance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Social Insurance Monthly Wage Lists and Annual Insurable-Earnings Declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly declarations and contributions by the 15th of the following month; annual insurable-earnings settlement by the close of the following February
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Statutory interest and fines on late contributions; employer criminal liability for falsified wage declarations; enforced collection against company assets for persistent defaults.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Audit is compulsory for all Egyptian LLCs irrespective of revenue or capital size: Law 159/1981 requires the annual appointment of at least one licensed auditor by the general assembly. Audited financial statements under Egyptian Accounting Standards must be presented to the annual ordinary general assembly and annexed to the corporate income tax return; Investment Law projects additionally file audited accounts with GAFI.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS), issued by the Ministry of Investment and substantially converged with IFRS; statutory books are prepared in Egyptian pounds under the EAS presentation requirements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: AML Law 80/2002 and its Executive Regulations oblige the LLC to maintain a beneficial-ownership register at the registered office and to identify any natural person directly or indirectly holding or controlling more than 25% of the quota capital or exercising ultimate control. The annual confirmation accompanies the commercial-register renewal documentation, and any transfer of quotas or change in control must be re-confirmed within 30 days of the underlying transaction. A nil-change confirmation remains obligatory even when no ownership movement occurred during the year.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $250–$650 per year (Egyptian agent-market range for a non-resident-owned trading LLC; excludes additional corporate-secretarial workload)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $800–$3,000 per year (certified audit fee for a mid-size off-price apparel wholesaler, dependent on turnover, inventory counts, and banking transactions)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Investment Law No. 72/2017 provides potential deductions on capital spending (not automatic tax holidays for wholesale trading); free-zone status can grant 0% CIT for qualifying activities; SME regime offers 5% rate on taxable profits up to EGP 20 million

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 9 (Corporate Income Tax Return for Joint Stock Companies and LLCs), filed electronically via the Egyptian Tax Authority portal (e.eta.gov.eg)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 4 months after the fiscal year-end; for a 31 December year-end, deadline is 30 April

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenues from sale of finished garments and off-price trade proceeds
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only Egypt-source revenues attributable to a permanent establishment; include FOB export sales if actually credited to Egyptian PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of goods sold and direct liquidation acquisition costs
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct only costs supported by arm's-length invoices; intercompany purchases must follow transfer pricing rules.
Allocate regional overhead costs to the PE on a justifiable basis and retain contemporaneous schedule.
Adjust for thin capitalization (30:1 debt:equity ratio) and controlled transactions adjustments.
Apply applicable DTA reductions if the PE remits profits to the head office; no branch remittance non-resident tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits: provisional payments, WHT, foreign tax credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach fixed deposit WHT certificates and foreign tax credit computation for export income taxed abroad.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing accrues a monthly delay surcharge of 2% of the tax due, plus a fixed penalty for non-submission; late payment triggers additional interest at the Egyptian credit rate plus statutory markup. Willful failure to file may produce a penalty of 50% of the assessed tax and criminal prosecution.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on distributions made to shareholders; dividends distributed to resident Egyptian companies are exempt from WHT under Law 91/2005
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Non-resident dividend recipient must submit a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by its jurisdiction, a beneficial ownership declaration, and a treaty-relief application to the Egyptian Tax Authority before payment. The Egyptian paying company may then apply the reduced treaty rate at source; otherwise, the excess can be recovered by filing an amended return or refund application within 5 years.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates: interest 20%, royalties 20%. DTAs commonly cap non-resident WHT at 5-15% for interest and 10-15% for royalties; a TRC is mandatory to invoke the reduced rate.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File required for aggregate controlled transactions exceeding EGP 10 million with a related party; Master File required where the multinational group's consolidated revenue exceeds EGP 500 million; CbC report required if group turnover exceeds EGP 25.6 billion.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egyptian tax law applies substance-over-form and GAAR; entities claiming treaty benefits or free-zone exemptions must demonstrate a real business presence including physical warehouse, Egyptian bank accounts, transfer of title/inventory, and decision-making in Egypt. Absent economic substance, transactions can be re-characterized and tax privileges stripped.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Dual sets of invoicing, cash sales of high-value off-price garments omitted from the official ledgers, or use of shell buyer entities to conceal turnover.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Law 91/2005, evaded tax is collected plus a 50% administrative penalty (doubled for repeat offending); criminal conviction carries imprisonment up to 5 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign the fraudulent return or knowingly omit income become jointly and severally liable for the tax, civil penalties, and risk travel bans and personal imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Payment of dividends, interest, or royalties to a non-resident beneficial owner without applying the statutory WHT and without filing the prescribed declarations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The paying entity is held liable for the unrecovered WHT, a 2% monthly delay surcharge on the underpaid amount, and a civil fine up to EGP 20,000 per return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Any director or senior officer accountable for the payment is personally liable for the withheld amount if it was deducted but not remitted; asset freezing and travel bans are commonly applied.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Engaging in cross-border transactions with related companies above the EGP 10 million threshold without preparing the Local File or using a non-arm's-length mark-up on liquidator merchandise.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authority may make an upward TP adjustment, impose a 10% additional tax on the adjustment amount, and apply a monthly delay penalty on the extra assessment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Officers who fail to ensure contemporaneous documentation are deemed primary tax violators under GAAR and can be jointly liable for the adjusted tax and penalty. In extreme cases, imprisonment for up to 3 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Registering an Egyptian LLC as a paper entity, without a physical office, warehouse, staff, or inventory, solely to route international off-price garment purchases and obtain treaty benefits or free-zone advantages.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Treble damage: denial of treaty benefits, retroactive revocation of free-zone tax holiday, re-qualification of transactions as taxable, and a fraud penalty up to 200% of the tax evaded.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Veil-piercing under commercial and tax law; shareholders/directors can be ordered to pay corporate debts and taxes from personal assets, and face criminal sanctions under Egyptian Companies Law.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Structuring cash deposits from liquidated garments into multiple bank accounts, using shell companies to layer payments, or accepting undeclared cash from unknown suppliers without adequate KYC checks.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: AML Law No. 80/2002 imposes a fine up to EGP 1,000,000 and imprisonment from 3 to 7 years; the funds and property derived from laundering are confiscated.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: In addition to criminal imprisonment, compliance directors face personal confiscation orders, disqualification from corporate office, and reputational travel bans upon indictment.
